title: Roadmap for the NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) | NIST

policy_extraction.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
covered_actors: Organizations designing, developing, deploying, or using AI systems (AI actors)
Subject matter experts and program evaluation experts

evidence.quote:
the goal of the AI RMF is to offer a
voluntary
resource to the organizations designing, developing, deploying, or using AI systems to help manage the many risks of AI and promote trustworthy and responsible development and use of AI systems.

Guidance on methods for developing reasonable risk tolerances.
NIST will work with the community to identify approaches organizations can use to develop risk tolerances.

Expanded TEVV efforts.
NIST will work with the broader community to develop tools, benchmarks, testbeds, and standardized methodologies for evaluating risks in AI and system trustworthiness, including from a socio-technical lens.

NIST intends to investigate how human-AI teams should best be configured to reduce likelihood of negative impacts/harms to individuals, groups, communities, and society. These impacts
may be related to human
insights
about AI-produced output, or human
oversight
of AI systems and their operation in real world environments.

Guidance related to explainability and interpretability, and how to apply that guidance within the AI RMF.
As our knowledge advances about how AI is understood across different audiences and for different purposes, NIST has identified a need to connect the field of AI explainability and interpretability more directly to AI risk management.

The Framework is intended to be voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector specific, and use-case agnostic, providing flexibility to organizations of all sizes and in all sectors and throughout society to implement the approaches in the Framework.
Organizations and individuals are encouraged to jointly or independently produce AI RMF profiles.

policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Companion NIST Roadmap outlining ten priority collaborative workstreams to advance AI RMF 1.0: international standards alignment/crosswalks (ISO/IEC 5338, 38507, 22989, 24028, DIS 42001, NP 42005), expanded socio-technical TEVV benchmarks/testbeds, sectoral and cross-sectoral Profiles (including hiring, criminal justice, lending, and LLMs), trustworthiness tradeoff guidance, RMF effectiveness evaluation, case studies, human-AI teaming/oversight guidance, explainability/interpretability guidance, risk-tolerance methods, and multidisciplinary tutorials. All workstreams are voluntary and contingent on available resources.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The AI RMF Roadmap is dominantly framed around innovation_enablement, setting out a flexible, voluntary, internationally aligned program of standards crosswalks, TEVV tools, profiles, case studies, and tutorials to close knowledge gaps and equip organizations to deploy trustworthy AI. Innovation_enablement leads consumer_public_safety, which is a strong secondary frame focused on reducing real-world negative impacts and harms to individuals, groups, communities, and society via TEVV, risk tolerances, and human-AI oversight. Fundamental_rights appears as a secondary rationale through the explicit 'rights-preserving' orientation and sectoral profile priorities covering hiring, criminal justice, and lending.
